description: Train transformer language models with reinforcement learning.

latest_release.name: v1.19.0
latest_release.body: ## Features ### 👥 Multi-teacher and agent distillation `DistillationTrainer` takes a dict of teachers, and each example's `teacher_id` column picks the one that scores its completion: the fusion stage of [MOPD](https://huggingface.co/papers/2606.30406). It also takes `environment_factory`, with the same contract as `GRPOTrainer`, so agents can be distilled against stateful environments. ```python trainer = DistillationTrainer( model="Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct", teacher_model={"math": "Qwen/Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B-Instruct", "code": "Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B-Instruct"}, train_dataset=dataset, # with a "teacher_id" column: "math" or "code" ) ``` * Implement MOPD for the `DistillationTrainer` by @cmpatino in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7215 * Add `environment_factory` support to `DistillationTrainer` by @sergiopaniego in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/8453 ### 🕐 Inkling 2 Mini Support for [`thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Mini`](https://huggingface.co/thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Mini): coverage in the VLM tests and an [example](https://github.com/huggingface/trl/tree/main/examples/sft_inkling_2_mini_clocks) that teaches it to read analog clocks. LoRA SFT on one H100 in 53 min takes it from 0% to **87.0% of held-out clocks read to the second**. Needs `transformers>=5.24.0`. * Add Inkling 2 Mini: tiny model, tests and clock-reading SFT example by @qgallouedec in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/8517 * Add a tiny Inkling 2 model and run it in the VLM tests by @qgallouedec in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/8498 * Add a tiny Inkling model by @albertvillanova in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/8512 ### ⚡ AsyncGRPO: faster packing, more architectures * **Plan and pack micro-batches with array operations**: on Qwen3-1.7B math rollouts (4×B300), planning + packing goes from 18 s to 1 s per pass, **+28% trained tokens/s**, with bit-identical batches. By @qgallouedec in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/8533 * **Nemotron-H tree packing**: Mamba2 layers (Nemotron-H, Granite-4.0-H, Bamba) now follow the tree, with new Triton tree scan, conv and fused mixer kernels. By @AmineDiro in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/8457 * **LFM in tree attention** by @younesbelkada in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7966 ### ✂️ 2x faster packed SFT with SDPA BFD packing (the default with `packing=True`) flattened the batch into one row, so SDPA attended across the whole batch: quadratic, and out of memory on Trainium. Packed examples now stay as rows, with `position_ids` restarting at each sequence. `padding_free=True` still flattens. s/step with `packing_strategy="bfd"`: | | v1.18 | v1.19 | | --- | --- | --- | | H100, Qwen3-1.7B, SDPA | 2.06 | **1.02** | | H100, Qwen3-1.7B, flash attention 2 | 0.828 | 0.832 | | Trainium2, Qwen3-0.6B, compiled | crashes | **3.2** | by @qgallouedec in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7804 ### 🛑 Fine-tuned models stop at the end of their turn Qwen base, Gemma 1/2 instruct, Qwen3.5 and a few others don't list their chat template's end-of-turn token as a stop token, so a model fine-tuned on them generated until `max_new_tokens`. `SFTTrainer` now adds that token to `generation_config.eos_token_id` when it's missing, and changes nothing elsewhere (checked on the 348 matching checkpoints among the 3000 most-downloaded Hub repos). by @albertvillanova in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/8565 ### 💬 More chat templates `assistant_only_loss=True` and tool calling work on more checkpoints, all by @albertvillanova: * Assistant-only loss: DeepSeek-V3.1 (#8431), DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp (#8471), DeepSeek-R1-Distill (#8529), SmolLM2 (#8444), Phi-4 (#8445), Gemma 4 (#8493), GLM-4.7 and GLM-5 (#8494), Qwen3-Coder (#8496), Llama 3.1 and 3.2 (#8495), OLMo 3 Think (#847

# TRL - Transformers Reinforcement Learning

A comprehensive library to post-train foundation models

## 🎉 What's New **⚡ AsyncGRPOTrainer is now stable:** [`AsyncGRPOTrainer`](https://huggingface.co/docs/trl/async_grpo_trainer) graduates to the stable API. It runs GRPO much faster by decoupling generation from training: a vLLM server streams rollouts while the trainer updates the model. ## Overview TRL is a cutting-edge library designed for post-training foundation models using advanced techniques like Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT), Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), and Direct Preference Optimization (DPO). Built on top of the [🤗 Transformers](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers) ecosystem, TRL supports a variety of model architectures and modalities, and can be scaled-up across various hardware setups. ## Highlights - **Trainers**: Various fine-tuning methods are easily accessible via trainers like [`SFTTrainer`](https://huggingface.co/docs/trl/sft_trainer), [`GRPOTrainer`](https://huggingface.co/docs/trl/grpo_trainer), [`AsyncGRPOTrainer`](https://huggingface.co/docs/trl/async_grpo_trainer), [`DPOTrainer`](https://huggingface.co/docs/trl/dpo_trainer), [`KTOTrainer`](https://huggingface.co/docs/trl/kto_trainer) and more. - **Efficient and scalable**: - Leverages [🤗 Accelerate](https://github.com/huggingface/accelerate) to scale from single GPU to multi-node clusters using methods like [DDP](https://pytorch.org/tutorials/intermediate/ddp_tutorial.html) and [DeepSpeed](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed). - Full integration with [🤗 PEFT](https://github.com/huggingface/peft) enables training on large models with modest hardware via quantization and LoRA/QLoRA. - Integrates [🦥 Unsloth](https://github.com/unslothai/unsloth) for accelerating training using optimized kernels. - **Command Line Interface (CLI)**: A simple interface lets you fine-tune with models without needing to write code. ## Installation ### Python Package Install the library using `pip`: ```bash pip install trl ``` ### From source If you want to use the latest features before an official release, you can install TRL from source: ```bash pip install git+https://github.com/huggingface/trl.git ``` ### Repository If you want to use the examples you can clone the repository with the following command: ```bash git clone https://github.com/huggingface/trl.git ``` ## Quick Start For more flexibility and control over training, TRL provides dedicated trainer classes to post-train language models or PEFT adapters on a custom dataset. Each trainer in TRL is a light wrapper around the 🤗 Transformers trainer and natively supports distributed training methods like DDP, DeepSpeed ZeRO, and FSDP. ### `SFTTrainer` Here is a basic example of how to use the [`SFTTrainer`](https://huggingface.co/docs/trl/sft_trainer): ```python from trl import SFTTrainer from datasets import load_dataset dataset = load_dataset("trl-lib/Capybara", split="train") trainer = SFTTrainer( model="Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B", train_dataset=dataset, ) trainer.train() ``` ### `GRPOTrainer` [`GRPOTrainer`](https://huggingface.co/docs/trl/grpo_trainer) implements the [Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) algorithm](https://huggingface.co/papers/2402.03300) that is more memory-efficient than PPO and was used to train [Deepseek AI's R1](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1). `accuracy_reward` needs math-verify, which you can install with `pip install trl[math_verify]`. ```python from datasets import load_dataset from trl import GRPOTrainer from trl.rewards import accuracy_reward dataset = load_dataset("trl-lib/DeepMath-103K", split="train") trainer = GRPOTrainer( model="Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct", reward_funcs=accuracy_reward, train_dataset=dataset, ) trainer.train() ``` > [!NOTE] > For reasoning models, use the `reasoning_accuracy_reward()` function for better results. ### `AsyncGRPOTrainer` [`AsyncGRPOTrainer`](https://huggingface.co/docs/trl/async_grpo_trainer) runs the same algorithm as [`GRPOTrainer`](https://huggingface.co/docs/trl/grpo_trainer), much faster: a vLLM server streams rollouts while the trainer updates the model, so generation and training overlap instead of alternating. The trainer needs vLLM and kernels, and `accuracy_reward` needs math-verify, which you can install with `pip install trl[vllm,kernels,math_verify]`. ```python # train_async_grpo.py from datasets import load_dataset from trl import AsyncGRPOTrainer from trl.rewards import accuracy_reward if __name__ == "__main__": dataset = load_dataset("trl-lib/DeepMath-103K", split="train") trainer = AsyncGRPOTrainer( model="Qwen/Qwen3.5-2B", reward_funcs=accuracy_reward, train_dataset=dataset, ) trainer.train() ``` Generation runs on a vLLM server, on a different GPU than the trainer. Start it on GPU 0: ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-2B \ --weight-transfer-config '{"backend": "nccl"}' --logprobs-mode processed_logprobs --max-model-len 4096 ``` Then run the training on GPU 1: ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 python train_async_grpo.py ``` ### `DPOTrainer` [`DPOTrainer`](https://huggingface.co/docs/trl/dpo_trainer) implements the popular [Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) algorithm](https://huggingface.co/papers/2305.18290) that was used to post-train [Llama 3](https://huggingface.co/papers/2407.21783) and many other models. Here is a basic example of how to use the `DPOTrainer`: ```python from datasets import load_dataset from trl import DPOTrainer dataset = load_dataset("trl-lib/ultrafeedback_binarized", split="train") trainer = DPOTrainer( model="Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B", train_dataset=dataset, ) trainer.train() ``` ### `KTOTrainer` [`KTOTrainer`](https://huggingface.co/docs/trl/kto_trainer) implements the [Kahneman-Tversky Optimization (KTO) algorithm](https://huggingface.co/papers/2402.01306), which aligns models from simple binary (desirable / undesirable) feedback rather than paired preferences. Here is a basic example of how to use the `KTOTrainer`: ```python from datasets import load_dataset from trl import KTOTrainer dataset = load_dataset("trl-lib/kto-mix-14k", split="train") trainer = KTOTrainer( model="Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B", train_dataset=dataset, ) trainer.train() ``` ### `RewardTrainer` Here is a basic example of how to use the [`RewardTrainer`](https://huggingface.co/docs/trl/reward_trainer): ```python from trl import RewardTrainer from datasets import load_dataset dataset = load_dataset("trl-lib/ultrafeedback_binarized", split="train") trainer = RewardTrainer( model="Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct", train_dataset=dataset, ) trainer.train() ``` ## Command Line Interface (CLI) You can use the TRL Command Line Interface (CLI) to quickly get started with post-training methods like Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) or Direct Preference Optimization (DPO): **SFT:** ```bash trl sft --model_name_or_path Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B \ --dataset_name trl-lib/Capybara \ --output_dir Qwen2.5-0.5B-SFT ``` **DPO:** ```bash trl dpo --model_name_or_path Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct \ --dataset_name argilla/Capybara-Preferences \ --output_dir Qwen2.5-0.5B-DPO ``` **KTO:** ```bash trl kto --model_name_or_path Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct \ --dataset_name trl-lib/kto-mix-14k \ --output_dir Qwen2.5-0.5B-KTO ``` Read more about CLI in the [relevant documentation section](https://huggingface.co/docs/trl/clis) or use `--help` for more details. ## Development If you want to contribute to `trl` or customize it to your needs make sure to read the [contribution guide](https://github.com/huggingface/trl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and make sure you make a dev install: ```bash git clone https://github.com/huggingface/trl.git cd trl/ pip install -e .[dev] ``` ## Experimental A minimal incubation area is available under `trl.experimental` for unstable / fast-evolving features. Anything there may change or be removed in any release without notice. Example: ```python from trl.experimental.new_trainer import NewTrainer ``` Read more in the [Experimental docs](https://huggingface.co/docs/trl/experimental_overview). ## Citation ```bibtex @software{vonwerra2020trl, title = {{TRL: Transformers Reinforcement Learning}}, author = {von Werra, Leandro and Belkada, Younes and Tunstall, Lewis and Beeching, Edward and Thrush, Tristan and Lambert, Nathan and Huang, Shengyi and Rasul, Kashif and Gallouédec, Quentin and Dirhoussi, Amine and Villanova del Moral, Albert and Paniego Blanco, Sergio}, license = {Apache-2.0}, url = {https://github.com/huggingface/trl}, year = {2020} } ``` ## License This repository's source code is available under the [Apache-2.0 License](LICENSE).
